project: ADR-062 — Capability Injection: Real Backends and Test-Harness-Only Nullifiers
description: Realization of ADR-062 (applying umbrella spec §17.17 unchanged). Every provider capability whose in-memory arm is a security NULLIFIER (key custody, device attestation, pre-rotation custody, DID/DHT resolution) gets a real production backend behind a dispatch seam, and its in-memory arm becomes a test-harness-only double gated `#[cfg(feature = "testing")]` (absent from shipped artifacts via G1's SOLE closed subset-allowlist); durability-only arms (storage, push, blob) stay legitimate explicit runtime options, never Default. The allow_in_memory_custody switch, the public custody=in_memory config, and the DidDht<D=InMemoryDhtClient> nullifier-default type parameter are all deleted. E4 relay-querier (`NoOpRelayQuerier`) is NOT a nullifier — it fails CLOSED (returns Ok(None), never a false document) and ships honestly as the DHT-only interim; its Slice 11 is a completeness/defense-in-depth fix (implement the real MultiRelayQuerier per §3.10.12). Units: UNIT 1 (Slice 0 module, Slice 1 DHT E1 incl. DidDht default removal + node DhtMode Memory->test-harness-only + fail-closed Disabled) executable now. UNIT 2 (pre-rotation on ACCEPTED ADR-054 + §9.7.4.1 item 3a: seam Slice 2, server floor Slice 3, interactive floor Slice 4, §5/§6 ceremony Slice 5; severance Slice 6; hardware backends Swift/Kotlin Slices 7/8, Python/TS FIDO2 Slices 12/13 — all as PRF-wrap-of-encrypted-offline compositions BLOCKED ON the upstream ADR-054 §4 hardware-wrap amendment, Slice 14). UNIT 3 (live SCP-CAPSEL fixes + completeness: E2 credentials Slice 9, E3 blob Slice 10 — impl-Default removals are live violations; E4 relay-querier Slice 11). #1733 folds and closes at Slice 6. Every capability is classified per §17.17.2 in the ADR.

stories.description: ADR-062 Slice 1 (Unit 1, E1 HIGH; §Decision 1 + D-A + D-B) — builds on SCP-CAPINJECT-000. STRUCTURAL ROOT FIX (D-A): in crates/scp-identity/src/dht.rs, remove the `= InMemoryDhtClient` default type parameter -> `pub struct DidDht<D: DhtClient, C: Clock = SystemClock>` (Clock default stays; SystemClock is not a nullifier), and DELETE `impl Default for DidDht<InMemoryDhtClient>` (:264) + the `pub fn new()` constructor (:270) that hardcode `InMemoryDhtClient::new()`. Every caller now constructs with an explicit DhtClient — PkarrDhtClient on production paths, InMemoryDhtClient only in `#[cfg(test)]`/`testing` code — so no silent in-memory DHT default is expressible (SCP-CAPSEL-8002 by construction). Blast radius (all in files[]): scp-identity/src/{dht.rs,config.rs}+Cargo.toml; scp-node/src/{self_host.rs,lib.rs,config.rs}+Cargo.toml; scp-runtime/src/discovery/{dht_context.rs,did_capabilities.rs}+Cargo.toml; scp-testing/src/helpers.rs+Cargo.toml; scp-ffi/common/src/{server.rs,resolvers.rs,bridge_instance.rs}; scp-ffi/{src,napi/src}/identity.rs; uniffi/src/bridge.rs (:3912/:8063/:9010/:9130/:16714 etc.). Then: `production-dht` unconditional on scp-ffi/napi/common; shared `enum FfiDhtClient` (Pkarr compiled unconditionally + `#[cfg(feature = "testing")] InMemory`); retype the chokepoints bridge_instance.rs:358 + server.rs:35 onto FfiDhtClient (the D-A removal compile-forces converting server.rs:455's `InMemoryDhtClient::new()` HERE, moved out of Slice 6); `ClientDhtConfig { gateways }` + `into_client -> Result<_, DhtInitError>` fail-closed; delete throwaway/fresh-per-call clients (scp-ffi/src/identity.rs, napi, uniffi make_dht_with_signer). D-B (node DhtMode reconciliation): `build_memory_did_method` builds DidDht<InMemoryDhtClient> used for BOTH publish and resolve, so DhtMode::Memory is a §17.17.3 resolve-nullifier -> make `DhtMode::Memory` test-harness-only (gated), add a new fail-closed `DhtMode::Disabled` (resolve returns a typed Err, never a silent in-memory no-op), and update construction.md M2's DhtMode::Memory-is-fail-safe text to name Disabled as the fail-safe no-publish value. scp-dht/testing wiring: gate InMemoryDhtClient's type behind a NEW `scp-dht/testing` feature; scp-dht stays a NORMAL dependency; each bridge/consumer `testing` feature carries `scp-dht/testing` as a NORMAL feature edge, and each consumer constructing InMemoryDhtClient in its own tests lists `scp-dht/testing` in ITS [dev-dependencies] (scp-node, scp-runtime, scp-testing) — `scp-dht/testing` MUST NOT appear in any default/non-testing feature list. Add matrix DHT rows. Closes #1518, re-satisfies #627, closes #1880. Scope exception: the default-removal + type-gate + chokepoint retype + node DhtMode split are atomic (partial application breaks the build).
acceptanceCriteria: The DidDht nullifier-default is removed (D-A): `grep -n 'DidDht<D: DhtClient = InMemoryDhtClient' crates/scp-identity/src/dht.rs` returns 0; `grep -n 'impl Default for DidDht<InMemoryDhtClient' crates/scp-identity/src/dht.rs` returns 0; and `grep -n 'pub fn new()' crates/scp-identity/src/dht.rs` returns 0 (the in-memory-hardcoding constructor is gone). The struct is `DidDht<D: DhtClient, C: Clock = SystemClock>`.

Every production caller constructs an explicit DhtClient; in-memory DHT appears only in test code: outside `#[cfg(test)]`/`#[cfg(feature = "testing")]`, `grep -rn 'InMemoryDhtClient' crates/scp-identity crates/scp-node crates/scp-runtime crates/scp-ffi` returns 0; the workspace compiles with the default-param removed (bare-production `cargo build --workspace` with no testing features succeeds and InMemoryDhtClient is out of scope).

production-dht unconditional on the three FFI crates: `grep -nE 'production-dht' crates/scp-ffi/Cargo.toml crates/scp-ffi/common/Cargo.toml crates/scp-ffi/napi/Cargo.toml` shows scp-dht pulled with production-dht in each dependency features list; no `[features]` entry makes it optional.

A shared `enum FfiDhtClient` (Pkarr unconditional + `#[cfg(feature = "testing")] InMemory`): `grep -n 'pub enum FfiDhtClient' crates/scp-ffi/common/src/dht.rs` matches, the InMemory arm is immediately preceded by that cfg, `grep -n 'allow_in_memory' crates/scp-ffi/common/src/dht.rs` returns 0, `impl scp_dht::DhtClient for FfiDhtClient` delegates publish/resolve.

InMemoryDhtClient type-gated behind a new `scp-dht/testing` feature wired as NORMAL edges (not cfg(test)): `grep -n 'testing' crates/scp-dht/Cargo.toml` shows the feature; the `pub struct InMemoryDhtClient` + impls carry `#[cfg(feature = "testing")]`; `scp-dht/testing` appears in each bridge/consumer `testing` feature list AND in the `[dev-dependencies]` of EVERY consumer that constructs `InMemoryDhtClient` in its own tests — scp-node, scp-runtime, scp-testing, scp-ffi, scp-ffi-napi, and scp-ffi-uniffi (grep each Cargo.toml); and `scp-dht/testing` appears in NO default/non-testing feature list (grep the Cargo.tomls to confirm it is only under a `testing = [...]` feature or `[dev-dependencies]`). This is the per-crate wiring that makes G1's soundness invariant hold: a consumer's `testing` feature transitively pulls the checked features, so shipped-graph feature-absence == type-absence.

Chokepoints retyped incl. server.rs:455: `grep -n 'type ConcreteDidMethod = DidDht<FfiDhtClient, SystemClock>' crates/scp-ffi/common/src/server.rs` and `grep -n 'dht_client: OnceLock<Arc<FfiDhtClient>>' crates/scp-ffi/common/src/bridge_instance.rs` both match; outside `#[cfg(test)]`, `grep -n 'InMemoryDhtClient::new()' crates/scp-ffi/common/src/server.rs` returns 0 (the :455 constructor converted here).

Throwaway/fresh-per-call clients deleted: outside `#[cfg(test)]`, `grep -nE 'InMemoryDhtClient::new\(\)' crates/scp-ffi/src/identity.rs crates/scp-ffi/napi/src/identity.rs` returns 0; the rotation_publish_client fallback and the uniffi make_dht_with_signer fresh-client are removed; an async test rotates a key and asserts a subsequent resolve through the shared resolver reflects the rotation.

Production DHT fails closed: `ClientDhtConfig::into_client` returns `Err(DhtInitError)` when Pkarr cannot be built; `grep -nE 'unwrap_or|or_else|InMemory' crates/scp-ffi/common/src/dht.rs` shows no in-memory/no-op substitution; a unit test asserts an unsatisfiable production config yields Err.

D-B node DhtMode reconciliation (variant + gate + default flip): `grep -n 'Disabled' crates/scp-node/src/config.rs` shows a new `DhtMode::Disabled` variant; `DhtMode::Memory` is gated `#[cfg(feature = "testing")]`; and the node/host_site defaults are flipped Memory->Disabled — `grep -n 'dht: DhtMode::Disabled' crates/scp-node/src/config.rs crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs` matches at both the NodeConfig default (config.rs:391 region) and the HostSiteConfig default (self_host.rs:976 region), and `grep -n 'dht: DhtMode::Memory' crates/scp-node/src/config.rs crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs` returns 0 outside `#[cfg(any(test, feature="testing"))]`.

A2 Disabled semantics — DHT-layer-off, resolver still composes the relay layer, fail-closed (NOT a typed Err on resolve, NOT a silent in-memory answer): a production (no-testing) test asserts that a `DhtMode::Disabled` node's resolution runs the `DualLayerResolver` with the DHT arm off and, with the interim `NoOpRelayQuerier` (pre-Slice-11) relay layer, returns honest not-found `Ok(None)` for an unknown DID (never a fabricated/in-memory document). (The relay-resolution positive path — a Disabled node resolving a peer published to a relay — is asserted in SCP-CAPINJECT-011 once the real MultiRelayQuerier lands; before that a Disabled node has no working resolution path, which matches and honestly improves on the old Memory default that silently resolved nothing.)

A1 construction.md M2 fully reconciled (no single-grep self-game): every M2 site that named `DhtMode::Memory` as the fail-safe no-publish value now names `DhtMode::Disabled` — check each of `.docs/standards/construction.md` lines ~:53 (the config-shape mapping), ~:63 (the Node/host_site M2 reasoning), ~:165 (`NodeConfig` field comment), and ~:194 (`HostSiteConfig`): `grep -n 'DhtMode::Memory' .docs/standards/construction.md` returns 0 references calling Memory the fail-safe/default value (Memory appears only where labelled test-harness-only), and `grep -c 'DhtMode::Disabled' .docs/standards/construction.md` is >= 4 (one per site, each naming Disabled the fail-safe no-publish value).

`python3.12 scripts/validate-prd.py` exits 0 with this story present.

Per ADR-054 §1: add the `PreRotationCustodyProvider` FFI callback interface (UniFFI [Trait, WithForeign] + PyO3 Py<PyAny> + NAPI TSFN) with the four canonical methods generate/public_key/import_seed_bytes/consume (mapped to the existing core `PreRotationCustody` trait methods per ADR-054's locked table — the core trait at traits.rs:740 is NOT renamed), and a `CallbackPreRotationCustody` adapter implementing the core trait with the single-use handle invariant. Because PreRotationCustody is RPITIT (traits.rs:759/772/782) the seam is an `enum FfiPreRotationCustody` — but to avoid front-loaded stubs the enum in THIS slice has ONLY `Callback(CallbackPreRotationCustody)` + `#[cfg(feature = "testing")] InMemory(InMemoryPreRotationCustody)` (the IndependentPrincipal arm lands with its KMS backend in Slice 3, EncryptedOffline with its backend in Slice 4). Delete the traits.rs doc-comment claiming InMemoryPreRotationCustody is the production default (a §3a violation). Add bridge-aliases.json entries for the per-binding-cased callback methods (else check-bridge-symmetry.sh trips). Add the pre-rotation-provider row to sdk-capability-matrix.json. stories.description: ADR-062 Slice 3 (Unit 2; §Decision 4, ADR-054 OQ2 §3a(a)) — builds on the seam (SCP-CAPINJECT-002). stories.title: UPSTREAM: ADR-054 §4 hardware-wrap amendment — specify the non-exporting-hardware (FIDO2/CTAP2/Secure Enclave/StrongBox) PRF-wrap-of-encrypted-offline realization and its §3a-conformance
stories.description: ADR-062 §Decision 4 (C6) — UPSTREAM design work, authored in a SEPARATE cryptographer cycle (NOT by the ADR-062 authoring pass). Accepted ADR-054 §4 lists FIDO2/U2F and hardware key stores as approved pre-rotation custody methods but does NOT specify how a NON-EXPORTING authenticator realizes the `PreRotationCustody` contract: FIDO2/CTAP2, Secure Enclave, and Android StrongBox cannot reveal or import a raw 32-byte private seed (that is the security property hardware custody exists to provide), so the `consume() -> seed` / `import_seed_bytes(seed)` reveal-and-import model does not fit them directly. The realization is a hardware-PRF-wrap-of-encrypted-offline COMPOSITION: the authenticator derives a stable per-credential KEK (FIDO2/CTAP2 `hmac-secret` / WebAuthn PRF; Secure Enclave / StrongBox key-agreement) that WRAPS an encrypted-offline seed (the seed lives in the §4 encrypted-offline codec; the hardware supplies the wrapping KEK in place of a user passphrase, and the hardware presence is the §3a-conforming independent principal). This story amends ADR-054 §4 to specify this model and establish its §9.7.4.1 item 3a-conformance (recovery-authority residence: the KEK is bound to the authenticator, an independent principal not reachable from operational custody), and lands any §9.7.4.1 spec clause if the amendment requires one (spec-first, per the artifact-flow invariant). This is the settled-upstream prerequisite for the four hardware backend stories (SCP-CAPINJECT-007/008/012/013), which are blockedBy it — a REAL forward dependency (the accepted §4 genuinely under-specifies non-exporting-hardware realization), not a deferral. It is UPSTREAM of those code stories per the artifact flow: the ADR/spec amendment settles before the SDK code that realizes it.
acceptanceCriteria: ADR-054 §4 (or a new amendment subsection) specifies the non-exporting-hardware realization: `grep -niE 'hardware.wrap|PRF.wrap|hmac-secret|non-exporting|wraps? .*(encrypted-offline|seed)' .docs/adrs/ADR-054-pre-rotation-custody-substrate-isolation.md` matches a subsection stating that FIDO2/CTAP2/Secure Enclave/StrongBox derive a wrapping KEK that wraps an encrypted-offline seed (no raw seed reveal/import), with the four canonical FFI methods (generate/public_key/import_seed_bytes/consume) mapped onto wrap/unwrap operations.

The amendment establishes §3a-conformance of the composition: the amended text argues the wrapping KEK's residence (bound to the authenticator, an independent principal not reachable from operational custody) satisfies §9.7.4.1 item 3a (grep the amendment for `item 3a`/`residence`/`independent principal`), and states which profile(s) each hardware backend conforms on.

If a spec clause is required, it is landed spec-first: either the amendment records that §9.7.4.1's existing text suffices (with the rationale), or a §9.7.4.1 clause is added in .docs/specs/09-security-model.md before this story is marked done (artifact-flow: spec before ADR before code).
The four hardware backend stories cite this amendment as their blocker: SCP-CAPINJECT-007/008/012/013 each list SCP-CAPINJECT-014 in blockedBy (verified by validate-prd's dependency check).
